definition: Friend (stylized as friend) is a wearable artificial intelligence device released by a startup company with the same name.
details: Avi Schiffmann, a Harvard University dropout, designed and released its first product in October 2023. Friend received significant backlash following a marketing campaign in 2025 that featured 11,000 advertisements in New York City.

explainer.lead: Friend is a wearable AI device made by a startup with the same name and first released in October 2023. It drew wider attention in 2025 when an 11,000-advertisement campaign across New York City prompted significant backlash.

tiers.eli5: Friend is an AI gadget made to be worn, a bit like a badge you carry around rather than a program you only open on a computer. Avi Schiffmann created it, and its first version came out in October 2023. Later, the company put up 11,000 advertisements in New York City, and the campaign received a lot of criticism.
tiers.practitioner: Treat Friend as a specific wearable AI hardware product, not as a model, algorithm, or software library. A technical evaluation would need device documentation before making assumptions about its sensors, interfaces, architecture, or integration options.
tiers.paperLevel: A plain-text record is: Friend := wearable AI device; developing company := Friend; first product release := October 2023; creator := Avi Schiffmann. Its documented public-reception event is a 2025 campaign comprising 11,000 New York City advertisements, followed by significant backlash; this establishes no technical performance claims.

explainer.example: A New York City resident encountering the campaign in 2025 would have been seeing one part of an 11,000-advertisement promotion for Friend. The scale of that campaign was followed by significant public backlash.

usedIn.name: Wearable AI
usedIn.detail: Friend belongs to the field of AI devices designed to be worn.

explainer.intuition: Friend is an example of AI packaged as a wearable consumer device rather than only as software on a computer or phone. Its history also shows how a product's advertising can become a major part of its public reception.
howItWorks: Avi Schiffmann, a Harvard University dropout, designed the startup's first product.
The product was released in October 2023 under the Friend name.
It took the form of a wearable artificial intelligence device.
In 2025, Friend promoted it through 11,000 advertisements in New York City.
That marketing campaign received significant backlash.
explainer.whyItMatters: Friend connects two notable aspects of consumer AI: putting the technology into wearable hardware and attracting public scrutiny through large-scale marketing. Its reception shows that attention generated by advertising need not be positive.
misconceptions: Friend is not the name of a general AI technique; it is a specific wearable device and the startup behind it.
Avi Schiffmann is described as a Harvard University dropout, not a Harvard graduate.
The 2025 controversy concerned a marketing campaign, not a documented technical failure of the device.
